metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 90), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +10% above peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.4) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 3–5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply 10–15% downward bias for first 7–10 days.  
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 2–4% for next 5 days.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.3) and price is volatile, model overfits noise; use 3-day rolling average to smooth forecast.
